# moddotplot-interactive v0.8.5

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.8.5 makes terminal exact plots easier to interpret without removing the v0.8.4
behavior. Exact plots now default to palette-based identity coloring, while the prior
A/C/G/T base coloring remains available through **Bases**. Users can also switch
between complete k-mer footprints and one-anchor-per-match geometry. These are display
choices over the same canonical exact-match inputs and are recorded in tile provenance.

The complete v0.8.4 source remains available beside this release for direct comparison
and rollback. Inside v0.8.5, selecting **Bases** with **Full footprints** preserves the
earlier base colors and match geometry while retaining the new explicit no-evidence
shade and explanatory legends.

See the [validation record](v0.8.5/VALIDATION.md) for the numerical, build, and browser
checks completed for this source copy.

## Exact display choices

At terminal zoom, **Identity** uses the active similarity palette and is the default.
**Bases** uses the categorical A/C/G/T colors from earlier versions and identifies the
X-axis base. An on-screen explanation reports the one-base cell size, canonical k-mer
length, selected geometry, and coloring semantics. Bases view includes its categorical
legend, and a shortcut exposes orientation coloring for repeat-rich comparisons.

**Full footprints** paints every aligned base in each matching k-mer and remains the
scientific geometry used by earlier releases. **K-mer anchors** paints one cell at each
matching canonical k-mer start pair, providing a conventional sparse-dot view without
silently changing the footprint interpretation.

Valid zero-identity or below-threshold cells retain the chosen plot background.
Positions without supporting exact k-mer evidence use a separate neutral shade and are
identified as “no k-mer evidence” in hover output. Image exports use categorical exact
legends rather than labeling binary exact-match states as a continuous `ANI_c` scale;
every exact legend includes explicit mismatch and no-evidence keys.

## Rendering and correctness

Exact integer textures use nearest-neighbor filtering and explicit integer texel
coordinates. The canvas backing buffer uses physical-pixel ResizeObserver dimensions
where the browser exposes them, with a device-pixel-ratio fallback. This keeps exact
cells deterministic across fractional CSS sizes while preserving the established
no-interpolation contract.

The exact core now defines even-k reverse-complement palindromes as ambiguous
orientation evidence and represents both possible footprint geometries. Numerical
goldens cover the 72 bp `(ACGT)18` repeat, full versus split-tile equivalence, anchor
geometry, and the even-k ambiguity case.

## Compatibility

Sketch estimation, loaded data, pairwise/grid ordering, feature tracks, and export file
formats/workflows are unchanged. Exact export legends and provenance reflect the chosen
view and geometry. Exact geometry changes require exact tiles to be recomputed but do
not reload the input FASTA or alter nonterminal sketch tiles.
